dimensions.note: No settings, vault refs or secrets. gh and git use the user's own auth (spec assumption). The tracked vault file is only local_encryption config with auto_generate, no key. CI's SWAMP_API_KEY/SWAMP_SIGNIN_TOKEN are template publish-dry-run secrets, not runtime ones.

merged_cleanup logs entry (what was asked), one line per PR and the summary; each cleanup_ method on @swamp/git and @webframp/github logs before and after. All use {placeholder} props; nothing sensitive logged. Covered by the logging tests in merged_cleanup_methods_test.ts and git_cleanup_test.ts.

Bad pr/prs and a non-GitHub origin throw before any write or call. Per-PR lookup failures become verdict error; in act a failed or throwing runModel call becomes that step failed and the result is still written. Pull failures split into skipped (cannot fast-forward) vs failed (network etc.); lease refusal (stale info) is skipped, other push errors failed. gh non-zero exit and non-JSON output give errors naming the command. The only broad catch (asked()) is for the log line and the method still throws.

make test: 82 passed, 0 failed. Tests run on real temp git repos with a bare origin; the @swamp/git built-ins are fakes, which I compared against the pulled @swamp/git source (status, branch list/checkout, pull --ff-only, remove_worktree without --force): same git commands and fields. Success and failure paths (dirty, locked, ahead, moved origin, network failure, throwing call, unknown commit, bad gh output) covered. Uses a hand-rolled context, not createModelTestContext; acceptable. The ask-once gate (AC13) has no test; checked by hand.

Worktree, local branch and origin branch already gone are reported as already done; a worktree removed earlier with its branch left is still verdict clean, so a rerun finishes a partial clean (tested: rerun after a failed origin delete). Main up to date is already done. Each step is independent, so an interruption leaves at most later steps undone, which a rerun picks up.

gh pr view/list JSON is validated with zod before use (missing state/head/branch is an error, never taken as closed). gh pr list is capped at 30 by latest activity and resorted by mergedAt, with truncated set when gh returned the full 30. repo is checked to be owner/name before being passed to gh.
Only Deno.Command(...).output() with stdin null, which collects and closes the pipes; no temp files or long-lived handles in the shipped code. Tests dispose their temp repos with await using.

Fixtures use acme/widgets, github.com/acme and example.com. README names no real repos or hosts. The recipe tags' source.url is the spec's loopback Capture address (127.0.0.1:3002), not real infrastructure. spec/ and CLAUDE.md are not in additionalFiles.

All schemas are plain z.object without passthrough. Mechanical checks: every writeResource call (result x3 instances, cleanupWorktrees, cleanupBranchHeads, cleanupBranchDelete, cleanupRemoteBranchDelete, cleanupMergedPrs, cleanupPullRequest) writes exactly its schema's fields, no placeholders; the one capped list (cleanupMergedPrs) has and sets truncated.
result: lifetime infinite, garbageCollection 20; the six helper resources on @swamp/git and @webframp/github: ephemeral, garbageCollection 10.
Not a CRUD lifecycle behavior: check/run read and clean acts once on git state it does not own; there is nothing to create, update or sync.

No declared swamp checks, but clean's safety checks are inline and per PR: the full check first, then again before each step (worktree branch, head, lock and status before removal; lease on the PR head for origin; main checkout branch and status before the pull; main checkout re-checked before a primary switch). Making these skippable by label would defeat the spec's no-orphan constraint, so inline is right.

Each method writes one instance: run->result, check->check, clean->clean, all the same ResultSchema. Helper methods write fixed or per-branch/per-PR names under their own specs; no collision within one execution.
No stored state is read back; every method reads git and GitHub afresh through context.runModel, which is right for a check-again-before-acting tool. No direct dataRepository access.
